This is just a small change to add frame_id when publishing the wrenches.

We need this in order to visualize (in rviz) the frame where the wrench applies to.

Just check and comment, do not merge it yet.
From the visualization i think that the force signs are reversed.
I'll check that tomorrow with the robot to make sure it's correct.

What i mean is, in order to be consistent with a force sensor on a robot, it should read as the force is being externally applied.
For me it seems that it is outputting the internal force instead, which is not what we want. But let me confirm this better.

author: the-mikedavis
body:
The JSONRPC spec says:

> If present, parameters for the rpc call MUST be provided as a Structured value

https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#parameter_structures

(Where a "Structured value" is elsewhere defined as either a map or array.)

This change skips the serialization of the `params` field for JSONRPC method calls and notifications if the `params` field is the `None` variant. This fixes compatibility with LSP servers which adhere closely to that part of the spec: `ocamllsp` in the wild.

Fixes #5400

author: mathieuimbert
body:
When using the newrelic bundle on Symfony 6.2 and PHP 8.1 I get the following error:

> Fatal error: Declaration of Ekino\NewRelicBundle\Logging\AdaptiveHandler::write(array $record): void must be compatible with Monolog\Handler\NewRelicHandler::write(Monolog\LogRecord $record): void in /var/www/html/vendor/ekino/newrelic-bundle/Logging/AdaptiveHandler.php on line 31

Since monolog/monolog `v3.0.0` the argument type was changed from `array` to `LogRecord` (see: https://github.com/Seldaek/monolog/blame/main/src/Monolog/Handler/NewRelicHandler.php#L60).

I updated the argument type, as well as the required version of `monolog/monolog` since the need to be compatible, it requires version `v3.0.0`.

Note I also reviewed that PR https://github.com/ekino/EkinoNewRelicBundle/pull/281 but I introduce less changes in the hope to fix that specific issue.

# Contributing to the Azure SDK

Please see our [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) if you are not familiar with contributing to this repository or have questions.

For specific information about pull request etiquette and best practices, see [this section](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-etiquette-and-best-practices).

## Description

Azure virtual network manager team is deprecating the API version associated with 20.6.1-Beta, 20.6.1-Beta.1, 20.6.1-Beta.2 of Azure Network management client library for .NET. Therefore, we need to add the deprecation announcement for these versions. Since there was no README for this library, I have added one with a section for the announcement, as recommended by Azure API release team https://dev.azure.com/azure-sdk/internal/_wiki/wikis/internal.wiki/192/Deprecation-strategy

author: ebroder
body:
This is my third crack at #1297, based on feedback from #1298.

When I dug into our logging infrastructure, I realized a few things. First, while the original idea of the "Ansible" library was to be able to log messages on the client that would also get seamlessly replicated to the server for persistence (i.e. FTL communication across the galactic space of the internet). In practice, we almost never used Ansible in client-side code (there were only about 5 call sites). Instead, for client-side code, we tended to use fine-grained `console.log` messages, which often supported being turned on or off at runtime for specific debugging cases.

Additionally, with the introduction of Bugsnag, we saw several cases where we wanted to both log an error and report that error to Bugsnag, leading to a fair amount of duplication of code of the form

```javascript
Ansible.error('Something went wrong', { error });
if (Bugsnag.isStarted()) {
  Bugsnag.notify(error, ...)
}
```

So...I pulled in a real grown-up logging library, [winston](https://github.com/winstonjs/winston#winston), which gives us enough capabilities to do all the things we need from logging today:

- We can transparently inject additional information to log messages, like automatically capturing `Meteor.userId` during method/publication invocations and adding it as log context on the server
- We can connect multiple log "transports", like having a Bugsnag transport that reports logs at the "warn" or "error" level if there's an error object attached to them
- We can have verbose log levels which aren't rendered by default. (Technically, we could do that before with `console.debug`, at least on the client-side, as browsers tend to not show that unless you explicitly opt in, but the messages still get rendered and stored)
- We can create child loggers with independent configuration so that we can turn (e.g.) debug logging on and off for `useCallState` independently of other debug logging. (Right now there's no easy way to get at that child logger to change it's configuration, but that was equally true of the old `DEBUG_LOGGING` variable.)

One thing I didn't do is convert `imports/client/tracing.ts` to use winston loggers, but it should be conceptually fairly straightforward.

In terms of review, 375204060587e5a83f28fb8612e040b7827bcb0c is quite voluminous; sorry about that. It's mostly rote conversions from either `console` or `Ansible` logging methods, but I did take the opportunity to clean up some of the message strings and additional contextual parameters, so it's not an automated conversion (or even a human-driven-automated conversion).

I'm also interested in feedback about whether this seems sophisticated enough that we could use this going forward in favor of overriding the `no-console` lint rule. (I'm not actively crusading over it, but I'm generally interested in keeping consistent downward pressure on eslint overrides in the codebase, either via improving our code style or by improving our eslint configuration)

Fixes #1297.

author: cruikshanks
body:
Testing against the environments was failing because the tear-down requests were returning an error. After investigating the issue we have found the requests are being rejected by the [Silverline WAF](https://www.f5.com/cloud/products/distributed-cloud-waf) used in our AWS environments because they don't have a body. For 'reasons' there is a policy to automatically reject POST requests with no body.

We're getting that changed but in the meantime adding a dummy body bypasses the issue. In getting this working we also found that the test data tear-down and setup actions take longer than the default 30 seconds in some of our non-prod environments. So, this change also includes an increase in the response timeout for those specific requests.

**Description**

Changes proposed in this pull request:

Created google workflow template for secrets leak detector.
Template is rendered by terraform with urls of cloud run services.
Workflow calls cloud run services which executes application logic.
Workflow is triggered by event arc trigger which transfers events published to pubsub topic.
All services accept requests in cloudevents format.
A tracing header `X-Cloud-Trace-Context` value is maintained between calls to subsequent services.
